scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

The imported 1600 to 1878 polygon is retained as map coverage, not a kingdom, language boundary, founding date or extinction. Geography around eastern Van Diemen Gulf and Awunbarna is compatible at a broad regional level only; geometry remains unverified.

National Library N47 confirms the Amarak, Amurdak and Umorrdak name association. Its Frank Clune manuscript is flagged secret/sacred and was not consulted or mined for practices. Public research written with Traditional Owner Charlie Mungulda supplies the cultural account.

The laundry-blue paper was downloaded from Griffith University and its full text inspected, particularly study area, methods, Table 1 and conclusion. Its lack of excavations is explicit; surface objects are not assigned invented dates. Adjacent Pleistocene sites do not prove an exact first-occupation date for these shelters.

Blue paint is treated as a documented adaptation of laundry whiteners, not a claim that Amurdak invented synthetic ultramarine or that the brand of every paint sample was chemically established. No medicinal use or restricted ritual instruction is reproduced.

The 2020 Painted Hands study was read in the ANU repository, including its definition, figure captions and interpretation. The horse establishes superimposition only. Interpretations of identity and cohesion are attributed, and neighbouring Gaagudju and Kuninjku practices are not assigned indiscriminately to Amurdak.

The 2026 boat paper was verified through its journal abstract; full-text download was unavailable. It reports an 1839 voyage by Alamurdie but proposes, rather than proves, his authorship. The entry year dates the voyage, not the rock paintings.

The 2026 Rainbow Serpent paper was read as indexed article text after direct access failed. It appeared online 14 August 2026 and was coauthored by Mungulda. Relative dating and a colonization-response hypothesis are separated. No restricted ceremonial sequence, site coordinates or unviewed image details are supplied.
The AIATSIS finding aid was read, not the original 1977 wordlist manuscripts. Lily Marriyulgij spelling follows the actual catalogue. No word translations are fabricated.

The Language Matters educational glossary was read; the documentary was not watched. Historical last-speaker statements are not converted into a current census, a death report or an assertion that the people are extinct.

Conference abstract and ANSTO booklet versions describe the same work; only one source is counted and no unpublished book is presented as already read. Independent depth review and geometry assessment remain pending.
